summary: Advance the solver in fixed dt while the display interpolates previous and current poses, and never feed the interpolated pose back into the solver.
objective: The solver steps a fixed positive dt; presentation interpolates completed states with a substep remainder; pause holds solver state and excludes paused wall time.
applies_when: A numerical solver and a variable display rate share the frame loop.
The viewer would see stutter if physics were shown only at completed steps.
intent_signals: smooth physics on a 144 Hz display
example_prompts: Step Rapier at 1/60 and interpolate body poses for the renderer.
Clamp catch-up steps so a hitch cannot spiral the solver.
negative_signals: Passing frameTime straight into the integrator as dt.
Writing interpolated poses back into the physics world.
not_for: Purely authored clips that already own presentation time.
Claims that a fixed step makes the engine scientifically valid.

principles: The renderer produces time; the solver consumes it in discrete dt slices. Leftover time stays in an accumulator.
Interpolation between previous and current solver state is a display trick. The simulated state remains the completed step.
A large hitch must be clamped or the solver spends the next frames catching up (the spiral of death). That clamp is a policy, not hidden magic.
implementation: Choose an explicit positive dt and a positive integer step cap. Rapier documents 1/60 s as its default; verify the installed binding and configure the intended value. While running, clamp incoming wall-frame time to the declared maximum and add it to the accumulator. Before each fixed-dt integration, copy current poses to previous; then step once, save current poses and subtract dt.

As an authored bounded catch-up policy, after reaching the step cap drop any remaining whole dt slices, retain only the substep remainder, and report the discarded time. Thus 0 <= accumulator < dt before alpha=accumulator/dt; lerp positions and slerp quaternions between previous and current states. Do not feed interpolated poses or alpha into the solver.

While paused, neither accumulate wall time nor integrate; hold the displayed pose and substep remainder. On resume reset the wall-clock baseline so paused duration is excluded. Reset restores body state, sets previous=current to that initial state, clears the accumulator and resets the clock baseline.

Report frame-time clamping and dropped backlog as simulation time intentionally not advanced. This policy can slow model time relative to wall time; it does not guarantee collision detection or remove the need for suitable dt and collision settings.
observable_checks: Changing display refresh does not change how far a freely falling body travels per second of model time, within the clamp policy.
A body moving at constant solver velocity appears between two completed poses rather than jumping a full dt when the display is faster than the solver.
Feeding interpolated poses into the next step is rejected: after pause, body translation matches the last completed step, not the blended mesh.

With a frame longer than the step budget, the chosen whole-backlog discard leaves alpha in [0,1), records dropped time and performs at most the cap. Pausing for a long interval adds no catch-up steps on resume.

creative_affordances: A ghost of the previous and next solver poses makes interpolation inspectable.
Slow-motion under the step cap can be presented as an honest performance mode.
known_limits: Gaffer's article is game-loop guidance; it does not certify a particular engine.
Rapier dt default 1/60 s is from the Rust integration-parameters page; verify the installed JavaScript binding.
Authored reusable guidance; no runtime artifact has been observed for this record.

claims.statement: A fixed-dt loop accumulates real frame time and integrates only with steps of size dt; leftover accumulator time is converted to an alpha in [0,1] used to interpolate previous and current physics state for rendering, including slerp of quaternions. A large frameTime should be clamped to avoid a spiral of death.
claims.scope: Glenn Fiedler, Fix Your Timestep! (2004); application loop design, not a particular engine's internals.

source_refs.locator: Free the physics accumulator loop; The final touch interpolation alpha = accumulator/dt; clamp frameTime

claims.statement: Rapier IntegrationParameters.dt is the timestep length used for each physics update, with default 1/60 seconds; smaller timesteps yield better accuracy and large timesteps increase linearisation error and may miss collisions of fast-moving objects.
claims.scope: Rapier Rust integration-parameters documentation; verify the installed JavaScript binding.
